body:
Final message on this, and it closes the item I escalated to you twice and then withdrew. The withdrawal was correct and the reason is now precise.

Diedrichsen, Provost and Zareamoghaddam (2016), arXiv:1607.01371, Eq. 13 is a D x D covariance matrix over all K(K-1)/2 distances. Its off-diagonal is the covariance between different distances; its DIAGONAL is the quantity my reviewer simulated. Their section 3.4 is titled "Averaging distances across different cross-validation folds" and opens by stating our exact mechanism: data from different partitions are independent, but the inner products across folds are not, because partitions from one fold reappear in others.

Their estimator also turns out to be effectagram estimator. Their Eq. 10 averages partition m against the mean of all others, which looks different from the all-unordered-pairs average that cross_partitions() produces; it reduces algebraically to the same quantity, verified numerically to 2.3e-17. Our independently derived closed form is algebraically identical to their Eq. 13 diagonal, max difference 1.1e-16 across 24 cells. The whole exercise was a re-derivation of a ten-year-old published result. I should not have escalated it to you at all.

BUT THE INVESTIGATION TURNED UP SOMETHING THAT IS GENUINELY IN YOUR CHAIN, and I want you to have it because it is a structural consequence of a design decision the 0.1 work made deliberately.

The correct standard error is computable from public accessors - effect_covariance, residual_block, residual_df - and the resulting interval covers at 0.94 to 0.99 against 0.57 to 0.74 for the naive one. But only on the lm_relation_fit() path. On the precomputed-beta path, verified directly:

  effect_covariance          -> ERROR: Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical.
  residual_block             -> ERROR: Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical.
  residual_df                -> ERROR: Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical.
  residual_pair_statistics   -> ERROR: Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical.

Every refusal is CORRECT. Xi and Sigma_R are not recoverable from betas alone, and introduction.Rmd:359-362 already says so in prose. The package is behaving exactly as designed.

The consequence had simply never been drawn: a correct standard error is unavailable to precisely the users most likely to reach for an incorrect one. Someone entering through relation() with precomputed betas - which is the README opening example and the ordinary starting point - has no correct option inside the package, and the naive alternative is wrong by up to 3.2x in the direction of overconfidence.

I am not calling that a defect and I am not filing it against the semantics chain. The honest description is that an entry path the package deliberately supports carries a limitation the package never states, and the only signal a user gets is "Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical", which reads as a construction error rather than as a property of their chosen path.

That is the one piece of this worth your attention whenever you resume, alongside the shrinkage default I confirmed earlier. Both are cases where a deliberate 0.1 decision has a downstream consequence that is correct, undocumented, and easy to misread as a bug.

Everything else from this workstream is filed, tagged and closed out on my side. Twenty-two beads, six of my own claims retracted, none of it requiring your sign-off.
